description:
Route single-matrix callers of the public $\mathbb{F}_3$ permanent entry point to the measured-faster kernel, and correct in the same change every piece of prose, benchmark label and artefact that the old selection made true.

## Background

`permanent_bipedal3` prefers the AVX2 single-word kernel whenever AVX2 is detected (`crates/gf2-algebra/src/permanent/bipedal3.rs:190-193`), and the SIMD feature is on by default, so every default build on an AVX2 host takes a path measured at roughly three times the scalar cost. No production code calls the dispatcher today; the penalty is paid by benchmarks, examples and research prototypes, and the campaign harness bypasses it by calling the single-word kernels directly.

The module's own documentation describes the current preference as intended, and `@/inv/single-source-prose` puts that correction in the same change as the code it describes: a reader of `bipedal3.rs` must not find a rustdoc comment contradicting the selection three lines below it. Prose living in other files — examples, benchmark labels, crate-level status text — is a separate sweep, because it is a different set of files with a different reviewer and no risk of contradicting the code beside it.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `permanent_bipedal3` selects the scalar single-word kernel for a single matrix, so a default build on an AVX2 host no longer pays the single-word SIMD penalty; the committed cross-CPU receipt putting scalar at $0.317$-$0.319$ of the AVX2 time is the measurement the selection rests on.
- [hard] REQ-02: Existing callers keep their results: the crate's permanent conformance tests, computer-algebra vector tests, and accelerator-versus-processor equivalence tests pass with their assertions unchanged.
- [hard] REQ-03: The rustdoc inside every file this change edits agrees with the selection it leaves in place, including the bipedal module documentation and the dispatcher's own documentation comment.
- [hard] REQ-04: A doctest or unit test pins the selection, so a later change that reintroduces the SIMD preference for a single matrix fails rather than passing quietly.
- [hard] REQ-05: Each modified SIMD source file has its sibling assembly artefact regenerated in the same change.

## Notes

The sampling campaign does not depend on this change, since campaign code calls the single-word kernels directly. It closes a defect every other caller of the public entry point silently pays for.
title: Dispatcher routing and prose sweep for the $\mathbb{F}_3$ permanent path
